stem: If there are 10 values each equal to 10, then S.D. of these values is : ______.
Number of patients who visited cardiologists are 13, 17, 11, 15 in four days then standard deviation (approximately) is
_note: DEFECT — no printed option matches the correct value. Mean \(= \frac{13+17+11+15}{4} = 14\); \(\sum x^2 = 804\), so variance \(= \frac{804}{4} - 14^2 = 201 - 196 = 5\) and S.D. \(= \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24\) patients. None of 5, 4, 10, 15 is \(\approx 2.24\). Option A (5) is the VARIANCE, not the S.D., so the book appears to have keyed the variance as though it were the standard deviation; A is recorded on that reading, but the question as printed has NO correct option. The four options are all distinct, so this is not a duplicated-option defect. Needs adjudication against the book's own answer key.
solution: [Textbook misprint: the question asks for the standard deviation of \(13, 17, 11, 15\). Their mean is \(14\) and the variance is \(\dfrac{20}{4} = 5\), so the standard deviation is \(\sqrt{5} \approx 2.24\) — which matches NONE of the four alternatives (5, 4, 10, 15), and 'approximately' cannot bridge \(2.24\) to \(4\). The keyed alternative, 5, is the VARIANCE. The sample convention does not rescue it either (\(\sqrt{20/3} \approx 2.58\)). The key is followed here as the setter's evident intent; the repair belongs to the stem (ask for the variance) or to the alternatives, not to the key.]

Following data gives no. of goals scored by a team in 100 matches. Compute the standard deviation.

| No. of Goals Scored | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No. of matches | 5 | 20 | 25 | 15 | 20 | 5 |
_note: DEFECT — the stem says 100 matches but the printed frequencies sum to \(5+20+25+15+20+5 = 90\), not 100. Transcribed exactly as printed; \(N = 90\) should be used for the computation.
solution: [Textbook misprint: the stem says 100 matches, but the frequencies in its own table sum to 90. Every other total in this exercise reconciles with its table, so this is a genuine internal inconsistency. Solved with \(N = 90\), which is also what the book itself used — its printed \(1.35\) is reachable only from \(N = 90\) (carried unrounded the value is \(1.34\)).]

Calculate coefficient of variation for the data given below

| Size (cm) | 5-8 | 8-11 | 11-14 | 14-17 | 17-20 | 20-23 | 23-26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No of items | 3 | 14 | 13 | 16 | 19 | 24 | 11 |

Compute coefficient of variations for the following data to show whether the variation is greater in the yield or in the area of the field.

| Year | Area (in acres) | Yield (in lakhs) |
|---|---|---|
| 2011-12 | 156 | 62 |
| 2012-13 | 135 | 70 |
| 2013-14 | 128 | 68 |
| 2014-15 | 117 | 76 |
| 2015-16 | 141 | 65 |
| 2016-17 | 154 | 69 |
| 2017-18 | 142 | 71 |
solution: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives the yield's coefficient of variation as \(5.91\). From the data, \(\Sigma y = 481\), \(\Sigma y^2 = 33171\), \(n = 7\), so \(\bar{y} = 68.7143\), \(\sigma^2 = \dfrac{836}{49} = 17.0612\), \(\sigma = 4.1305\) and \(C.V. = \dfrac{100 \times 4.1305}{68.7143} = 6.011\). No rounding path reaches \(5.91\) — that value would require \(\sigma = 4.061\) — so it reads as a digit slip from \(6.01\). The book's area \(C.V. = 9.21\) is correct and its conclusion is unaffected, since \(9.21\) exceeds the yield figure either way.]
